param18.title: F.ENV
param18.summary: How far each note sweeps the filter.
param18.does: The filter envelope opens (positive) or closes (negative) the cutoff by up to 6 or -4 octaves on every note, following F.ATK, F.DEC and F.SUS. 0 means no sweep.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param18.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Positive F.ENV with short F.DEC gives a plucky wow.
param18.ask: What does F.ENV do to the sound?

param19.title: F.ATK
param19.does: How long the filter takes to reach its peak sweep after a note starts, 1 ms to 4 s. Longer gives a slow brightening.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param19.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Only audible when F.ENV is not 0.
param19.ask: What does F.ATK do to the sound?

param20.title: F.DEC
param20.does: How long the filter takes to fall from its peak to the F.SUS level, 10 ms to 6 s. Short is a quick pluck; long is a slow fade of brightness.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param20.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Only audible when F.ENV is not 0.
param20.ask: What does F.DEC do to the sound?

param21.title: F.SUS
param21.does: How much of the sweep stays while the key is held, 0 to 100%. At 0 the filter returns to the base CUTOFF; at 100% it stays fully open.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param21.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Only audible when F.ENV is not 0.
param21.ask: What does F.SUS do to the sound?

param22.title: F.REL
param22.does: How the filter moves after you let go, 10 ms to 8 s. Short snaps the brightness shut; long lets it close slowly with the tail.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param22.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Only audible when F.ENV is not 0.
param22.ask: What does F.REL do to the sound?

param23.title: K.TRACK
param23.does: Key tracking: 0 keeps the cutoff fixed; 100% moves it one octave for every octave you play, so high notes stay as bright as low ones. Middle C (C4) is the pivot.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param23.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 2/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Low K.TRACK makes high notes dull.
param23.ask: What does K.TRACK do to the sound?

param24.title: VIB HZ
param24.does: How fast vibrato, the pitch wobble, cycles: 0.5 to 9 times a second. Slow is a gentle waver; fast is a nervous shake. Only audible when VIBRATO is above 0.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param24.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: 5 to 6 Hz sounds like a singer.
param24.ask: What does VIB HZ do to the sound?

param25.title: VIBRATO
param25.does: How far the pitch wobbles each side, 0 to 60 cents (100 cents is one semitone). The Wobble touch pad mapping adds extra vibrato live, on top of this.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param25.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: 5 to 10 cents is subtle and expressive.
param25.ask: What does VIBRATO do to the sound?

param26.title: VIB DLY
param26.does: Seconds, 0 to 2, before the vibrato starts after a note begins; it then fades in over a quarter second. Like a singer holding a note straight, then wavering.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param26.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Zero gives vibrato from the first instant.
param26.ask: What does VIB DLY do to the sound?

param27.title: LFO HZ
param27.does: The LFO (low-frequency oscillator) is a slow wobble generator, 0.05 to 12 times a second. It drives LFO>CUT, LFO>AMP and LFO>WID, so nothing is heard unless one of them is above 0.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param27.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Match the delay: 1 Hz is one wobble a second.
param27.ask: What does LFO HZ do to the sound?

param28.title: LFO>CUT
param28.does: How many octaves the LFO swings the cutoff, 0 to 3. Gives a wah-wah or breathing brightness at the LFO HZ rate. 0 is off.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param28.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Slow LFO HZ with LFO>CUT 1 sounds like a pad breathing.
param28.ask: What does LFO>CUT do to the sound?

param29.title: LFO>AMP
param29.does: Tremolo: the LFO makes the volume pulse, 0 to 100% deep. Slow is a gentle swell; fast is a shudder. 0 is off.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param29.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Keep it under 30% for a subtle shimmer.
param29.ask: What does LFO>AMP do to the sound?

param30.title: LFO>WID
param30.does: How much the LFO moves the square wave's WIDTH, 0 to 40%. It makes a moving, chorus-like tone, and only affects SQUARE waves.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param30.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Set WAVE A to SQUARE first.
param30.ask: What does LFO>WID do to the sound?

param31.title: GLIDE
param31.does: Portamento: how long the pitch takes to travel when you slide from one note to another, 0 to 2000 ms. Short is a quick snap; long is a slow, swooping slide. Tune's Glide speed scales every sound.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param31.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.3/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: 0 gives instant jumps without a slide.
param31.ask: What does GLIDE do to the sound?

param32.title: DRIVE
param32.does: Saturation squashes the wave: 0 is clean, low is warm, high is gritty and fuzzy. The Morph touch pad mapping adds drive live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param32.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.3/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Drive adds loudness; watch the Limit tag.
param32.ask: What does DRIVE do to the sound?

param33.title: CHORUS
param33.does: Chorus doubles the sound with a slightly detuned, wavering copy, so it sounds wider and shimmering. 0 is off, 100% is a thick swirl.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param33.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Chorus and reverb together sound big.
param33.ask: What does CHORUS do to the sound?

param34.title: DELAY
param34.does: Delay repeats the sound after a pause, 0 to 70%. Echo spacing follows the tempo: set it with DLY TIME. The X axis of the Space touch pad mapping adds delay live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param34.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.3/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Slow, sparse playing sounds best with echoes.
param34.ask: What does DELAY do to the sound?

param35.title: DLY TIME
param35.does: Chooses how long the echo waits, locked to the tempo: 1/16, 1/16 dotted, 1/8, 1/8 dotted or 1/4 note (one beat). Slower tempo means longer gaps.

use.text: Drag along the bar: it clicks through its steps; the name shows at the right.

param35.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 3/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: 1/8 dotted is the classic rhythmic echo.
param35.ask: What does DLY TIME do to the sound?

param36.title: DLY FB
param36.does: Feedback: how much of each echo is fed back in, 0 to 80%. Low gives one or two repeats; high gives a long trail that fades slowly.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param36.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Has no effect when DELAY is 0.
param36.ask: What does DLY FB do to the sound?

param37.title: REVERB
param37.does: Reverb adds the sense of a space, 0 to 80%. Low is a small room; high washes the sound out. The Y axis of the Space touch pad mapping adds reverb live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param37.recall: Sound page, quick sliders (also All parameters p.4/4). Re-tap the sound's slot to reload it.
tips: Pull this down if the sound feels washed out.
param37.ask: What does REVERB do to the sound?

param38.title: REV SIZE
param38.does: How big the room is, 20 to 98%: small is a quick tight tail; large is a long, drifting tail. Needs REVERB above 0 to be heard.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param38.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: Large size with low REVERB is a subtle halo.
param38.ask: What does REV SIZE do to the sound?

param39.title: LEVEL
param39.does: A volume trim in decibels, about -34 dB to +12 dB, so different sounds sit at similar loudness. Random sounds set it for you. Master volume (System page) is separate.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar; the value shows at the right.

param39.recall: Sound > All parameters, page 4/4. Re-tap the sound's slot to reload the saved version.
tips: If the Limit tag shows, lower this or Master volume.
param39.ask: What does LEVEL do to the sound?

sound-deep.recall: Sound tab, then All parameters. Prev and Next turn the four pages.

beat.title: Beat
beat.intro: A drum machine: eight pads, three kits, one bar of 16 steps written by playing, and a row of kept beats.

tab_track.title: PAGE TABS
tab_track.summary: The strip of nine tabs along the top.
tab_track.does: Track, Synth, Sound, Beat, Backing, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_track.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all nine; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_track.ask: What is on each of the pages?

pad0.title: PAD 1: KICK
pad0.does: A short low thump: the bass drum that anchors the beat. Usually on steps 1 and 9 of the bar for a steady pulse. Tap or press its key to hear it. With Rec on, each hit is written into the bar at the nearest of 16 steps.

use.text: Tap the pad; it flashes when its drum sounds.
Press Q or U (two keys so you can repeat fast).
With Erase armed, tap the pad to clear that drum's hits.

pad0.recall: Beat page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Beat page. Erase then this pad clears just its hits.
tips: The pad row of the grid above lights where its hits sit.
pad0.ask: How do I get the kick into my beat?

pad1.title: PAD 2: SNARE
pad1.does: A bright crack with a short noisy tail. Classically on the second and fourth beats of the bar. Tap or press its key to hear it. With Rec on, each hit is written into the bar at the nearest of 16 steps.

use.text: Tap the pad; it flashes when its drum sounds.
Press W or I (two keys so you can repeat fast).
With Erase armed, tap the pad to clear that drum's hits.

pad1.recall: Beat page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Beat page. Erase then this pad clears just its hits.
tips: The pad row of the grid above lights where its hits sit.
pad1.ask: How do I get the snare into my beat?

pad2.title: PAD 3: HAT
pad2.does: A very short, thin metallic tick. Played on every step it gives a steady ticking pulse; off-beat hits are a little quieter. Tap or press its key to hear it. With Rec on, each hit is written into the bar at the nearest of 16 steps.

use.text: Tap the pad; it flashes when its drum sounds.
Press E or O (two keys so you can repeat fast).
With Erase armed, tap the pad to clear that drum's hits.

pad2.recall: Beat page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Beat page. Erase then this pad clears just its hits.
tips: The pad row of the grid above lights where its hits sit.
pad2.ask: How do I get the hat into my beat?

pad3.title: PAD 4: OPEN HAT
pad3.does: A hi-hat left open: a longer sizzle that rings out. Often placed between kicks, on the off-beats. Tap or press its key to hear it. With Rec on, each hit is written into the bar at the nearest of 16 steps.

use.text: Tap the pad; it flashes when its drum sounds.
Press R or P (two keys so you can repeat fast).
With Erase armed, tap the pad to clear that drum's hits.

pad3.recall: Beat page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Beat page. Erase then this pad clears just its hits.
tips: The pad row of the grid above lights where its hits sit.
pad3.ask: How do I get the open hat into my beat?

pad4.title: PAD 5: CLAP
pad4.does: A short burst of noise like hands clapping. Layer it with the snare or use it instead. Tap or press its key to hear it. With Rec on, each hit is written into the bar at the nearest of 16 steps.

use.text: Tap the pad; it flashes when its drum sounds.
Press A or H (two keys so you can repeat fast).
With Erase armed, tap the pad to clear that drum's hits.

pad4.recall: Beat page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Beat page. Erase then this pad clears just its hits.
tips: The pad row of the grid above lights where its hits sit.
pad4.ask: How do I get the clap into my beat?

pad5.title: PAD 6: RIM
pad5.does: A dry, sharp click like a stick on the rim of a snare. Good for quiet, sparse patterns. Tap or press its key to hear it. With Rec on, each hit is written into the bar at the nearest of 16 steps.

use.text: Tap the pad; it flashes when its drum sounds.
Press S or J (two keys so you can repeat fast).
With Erase armed, tap the pad to clear that drum's hits.

pad5.recall: Beat page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Beat page. Erase then this pad clears just its hits.
tips: The pad row of the grid above lights where its hits sit.
pad5.ask: How do I get the rim into my beat?

pad6.title: PAD 7: TOM
pad6.does: A rounded, pitched drum hit, lower than the snare. Good for fills and rolls around the bar's end. Tap or press its key to hear it. With Rec on, each hit is written into the bar at the nearest of 16 steps.

use.text: Tap the pad; it flashes when its drum sounds.
Press D or K (two keys so you can repeat fast).
With Erase armed, tap the pad to clear that drum's hits.

pad6.recall: Beat page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Beat page. Erase then this pad clears just its hits.
tips: The pad row of the grid above lights where its hits sit.
pad6.ask: How do I get the tom into my beat?

pad7.title: PAD 8: COWBELL
pad7.does: A bright metallic ringing clank. Use it sparingly as an accent or on the off-beats. Tap or press its key to hear it. With Rec on, each hit is written into the bar at the nearest of 16 steps.

use.text: Tap the pad; it flashes when its drum sounds.
Press F or L (two keys so you can repeat fast).
With Erase armed, tap the pad to clear that drum's hits.

pad7.recall: Beat page, pad grid. Keys work only on the Beat page. Erase then this pad clears just its hits.
tips: The pad row of the grid above lights where its hits sit.
pad7.ask: How do I get the cowbell into my beat?

beatslot0.title: KEPT BEATS
beatslot0.summary: Your beats in a row. Tap one to switch to it.
beatslot0.does: Every beat you make is kept in this row, each with its own kit; changes are saved as you go. While the beat plays, a tapped beat waits for the next bar line, then takes over in time. Stopped, it switches at once.

use.text: Tap a beat; it waits for the next bar.
Left / Right: the beat before or after.

beatslot0.recall: Beat page, row under the pads. A beat cannot be deleted or renamed yet; Left/Right moves along the row.
tips: The tempo and beat volume are shared by every beat.
beatslot0.ask: How do I keep several beats and switch between them?

beatnew.title: + NEW BEAT
beatnew.summary: Starts an empty beat and keeps the one you have.
beatnew.does: Adds a fresh empty beat to the row, using the kit you have now, and switches to it. Your previous beat is kept. If the beat shown is already empty it does nothing, so you cannot stack empty beats.

use.text: Tap + New, then play pads with Rec on.

beatnew.recall: Beat page, at the end of the kept-beats row. Go back by tapping the older beat or pressing Left.
tips: Nothing to save by hand: beats are kept for you a moment after each change.
beatnew.ask: How do I start a second beat without losing the first?

beatmore.title: MORE BEATS
beatmore.summary: Shows the next page of kept beats.
beatmore.does: With more than seven beats the row shows six a page, plus More and + New. More turns the page and wraps back to the first after the last.

use.text: Tap More to step through the pages.

beatmore.recall: Beat page, row under the pads, only once you have more than seven beats.
beatmore.ask: Where do my older beats go once the row fills?

beatrec.title: REC
beatrec.summary: Writes the pads you play into the bar.
beatrec.does: On: the beat starts, the metronome clicks, and each pad hit is written at the nearest of the 16 steps in the bar (that is quantising: snapping to the grid). Next time round it plays back. Off: pads play without changing the beat.

use.text: Tap Rec; inverted means recording.
Enter here, or Ctrl+I anywhere.

beatrec.recall: Beat page, transport row. Ctrl+I anywhere. Stopping the beat also switches Rec off. Erase fixes mistakes.
tips: Late on Bluetooth? System page, Loop fix.
beatrec.ask: How do I record a drum pattern in time?

beatplay.title: PLAY / STOP BEAT
beatplay.does: Plays the 16-step bar on a loop at the current tempo, sharing bar lines with the backing chords and loop pedal so everything stays together. Stopping also turns Rec off.

use.text: Tap Play or Stop.
Space on this page, or Ctrl+J from any page.

beatplay.recall: Beat page, transport row. Ctrl+J anywhere. Starting the Track stops the live beat.
beatplay.ask: Why does the beat start in time with my loop?

beaterase.title: ERASE
beaterase.summary: Clears one drum's hits from the bar.
beaterase.does: Tap Erase (pads now say erase), then tap the pad of the drum to clear. Only that drum's hits go; the other drums stay. It disarms after one use.

use.text: Tap Erase, then tap a pad. Tap Erase again to cancel.

beaterase.recall: Beat page, transport row. No undo: re-record the hits. Tapping a tab disarms it.
tips: To clear everything, start a + New beat instead.
beaterase.ask: How do I remove just the hi-hats?

kit-.title: KIT
kit-.summary: Chooses the drum sounds: Soft, Crunchy or Glitchy.
kit-.does: Soft is round and quiet with a little room. Crunchy is driven and lo-fi. Glitchy has zaps and crushed noise. − and + step through them and wrap around. A kept beat remembers its kit.

use.text: Tap − or + to change kit.

kit-.recall: Beat page, right of Erase. In the Track, change a beat clip's kit with Sound.
tips: A beat clip on the Track keeps its own kit; change it there with Sound.
kit-.ask: What is the difference between the three kits?

beatvol.title: BEAT VOLUME
beatvol.does: Volume of the drum machine only, 0-100%, shared by all kept beats. Master volume on the System page sets the overall level.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar.

beatvol.recall: Beat page, bottom left. Master volume: System page.
tips: Loud pads with Glitch? Glitch also crushes the drums.
beatvol.ask: How do I make the drums quieter than the synth?

bpm3-.title: TEMPO
bpm3-.summary: The tempo in beats per minute.
bpm3-.does: Sets the speed of everything: beat, backing, loop and track. 40 to 240 bpm; each tap changes it by 1. It is the same setting as on the Tune and Backing pages.

use.text: Tap − or +.
Ctrl+T taps a tempo.

bpm3-.recall: Beat page bottom right; Tune page, Tempo (steps of 1) or Tap. Ctrl+T.
bpm3-.ask: How do I change the tempo?

beat.recall: Beat tab. Ctrl+J starts or stops the beat from any page; Ctrl+I toggles Rec.

backing.title: Backing
backing.intro: Backing chords from your key: pick what a chord tap does, how they play, and how long each lasts.

tab_track.title: PAGE TABS
tab_track.summary: The strip of nine tabs along the top.
tab_track.does: Track, Synth, Sound, Beat, Backing, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_track.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all nine; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_track.ask: What is on each of the pages?

bmode0.title: PROGRESSION MODE
bmode0.summary: Chord taps build a looping progression.
bmode0.does: A chord tap adds to a looping sequence of up to eight chords. Tap Play (or the first chord) to hear it loop.

use.text: Tap chords in order to fill the strip.
Ctrl+B cycles the mode.

bmode0.recall: Backing page, top row; Synth page, mode button by the pads. Ctrl+B cycles Prog, Hold, Drone.
bmode0.ask: When would I use progression mode?

bmode1.title: HOLD MODE
bmode1.summary: Chord taps latch a single chord.
bmode1.does: A chord tap plays that one chord until you pick another. Tap the same chord again to stop it.

use.text: Tap a chord pad to latch it.
Ctrl+B cycles the mode.

bmode1.recall: Backing page, top row; Synth page, mode button by the pads. Ctrl+B cycles Prog, Hold, Drone.
bmode1.ask: When would I use hold mode?

bmode2.title: DRONE MODE
bmode2.summary: Chord taps latch a drone note.
bmode2.does: A chord tap switches a held bass note for that chord on or off. Several drones can sound at once.

use.text: Tap pads to add or remove drone notes.
Ctrl+B cycles the mode.

bmode2.recall: Backing page, top row; Synth page, mode button by the pads. Ctrl+B cycles Prog, Hold, Drone.
tips: A drone is the chord's root note, an octave up.
bmode2.ask: When would I use drone mode?

bstyle0.title: SUSTAIN STYLE
bstyle0.summary: Chord notes ring continuously, gliding to the next chord.
bstyle0.does: All notes of the chord are held for the whole chord length; when the chord changes the notes slide to the new ones. The calmest style, good under slow playing.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle0.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
bstyle0.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bstyle1.title: PULSE STYLE
bstyle1.summary: The chord re-strikes on every beat.
bstyle1.does: The root is held while the upper notes of the chord are struck short on every beat, like a steady organ or guitar chop.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle1.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
bstyle1.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bstyle2.title: ARP UP STYLE
bstyle2.summary: Chord notes play one by one, upward.
bstyle2.does: An arpeggio: the chord's notes are played one at a time, climbing across two octaves and starting over. Speed is set by steps per beat.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle2.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
tips: Arp steps per beat is the stepper below.
bstyle2.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bstyle3.title: ARP DOWN STYLE
bstyle3.summary: Chord notes play one by one, downward.
bstyle3.does: An arpeggio running downward through the chord's notes across two octaves, then starting again. Speed is steps per beat.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle3.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
tips: Arp steps per beat is the stepper below.
bstyle3.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bstyle4.title: ARP UP-DN STYLE
bstyle4.summary: Chord notes climb then fall, back and forth.
bstyle4.does: An arpeggio that climbs to the top of the two-octave span, turns round and falls back down, repeating. Speed is steps per beat.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active style is inverted.
Ctrl+A steps through the five styles.

bstyle4.recall: Backing page, second row. Ctrl+A steps Sustain, Pulse, Arp up, Arp down, Arp up-dn.
tips: Arp steps per beat is the stepper below.
bstyle4.ask: How do the backing styles differ?

bslot0.title: PROGRESSION SLOTS
bslot0.summary: The chords you queued, up to eight. Tap to select one.
bslot0.does: Each filled slot shows a chord name; the playing one is inverted. Tap a slot to select it (double frame), then tap a chord pad to replace it. Tap the selected slot again to deselect.

use.text: Tap a filled slot, then a chord pad to swap it.

bslot0.recall: Backing page, progression row; also Synth page. Ctrl+Backspace removes the last chord.
tips: Empty slots show only their number and cannot be tapped.
bslot0.ask: How do I change one chord in my progression?

bremove.title: REMOVE LAST
bremove.summary: Takes the last chord off the progression.
bremove.does: Deletes the last chord in the queue, one per tap. The rest keep playing. Does not touch the held chord or drones.

use.text: Tap Remove last.
Ctrl+Backspace.

bremove.recall: Backing page, first row of buttons. Ctrl+Backspace. To replace instead, tap a slot then a chord.
bremove.ask: How do I drop the last chord I added?

bclear.title: CLEAR ALL
bclear.does: Removes every chord, the held chord and all drones, and stops the backing. Does not touch the loop, beat or track.

use.text: Tap Clear all.
Ctrl+X.

bclear.recall: Backing page. Ctrl+X anywhere (on the Track page Ctrl+X cuts a clip instead). No undo: tap the chords again.
bclear.ask: How do I start the backing chords over?

bseventh.title: 7TH CHORDS
bseventh.does: Off: three-note triads. On: four-note seventh chords, which sound richer and more jazzy. Pad names update to match. Applies to everything the backing plays.

use.text: Tap to switch; inverted means on.

bseventh.recall: Backing page, third button. Tap again to go back to triads.
bseventh.ask: What does 7th chords change in the sound?

bmetro.title: METRONOME
bmetro.does: Plays a quiet click in time with the tempo, louder on the first beat of each bar. The count-in click always sounds regardless, and Rec on the Beat page clicks too.

use.text: Tap to switch; also Click on the Tune page.
Ctrl+M.

bmetro.recall: Backing page and Tune page (Click); Ctrl+M. It is one shared setting.
bmetro.ask: How do I turn the click on?

chord0.title: CHORD PADS I-VII
chord0.summary: The seven chords of your key; what a tap does depends on mode.
chord0.does: Each pad shows a chord and its numeral (small = minor). Prog: a tap adds it to a looping progression of up to eight. Hold: latches one chord. Drone: toggles its root as a held note.

use.text: Tap a pad. Mode: the button beside the pads.
Alt+Z..M: chords I to VII.

chord0.recall: Synth and Backing pages. Ctrl+X clears; Ctrl+Backspace removes the last chord.
tips: Chords follow the key and scale.
chord0.ask: What do the chord pads do in each mode?

backmode.title: CHORD MODE
backmode.summary: Prog, Hold or Drone: what a chord tap does.
backmode.does: Prog adds taps to a looping progression. Hold plays one chord until you pick another (tap it again to stop). Drone switches a held bass note for each chord you tap on and off.

use.text: Tap to step Prog, Hold, Drone.
Ctrl+B steps the mode.

backmode.recall: Synth page, beside the pads; three buttons on the Backing page. Ctrl+B steps it.
tips: Mode names appear as a toast when you use Ctrl+B.
backmode.ask: What is the difference between Prog, Hold and Drone?

backplay.title: BACKING PLAY / STOP
backplay.summary: Starts and stops the backing chords.
backplay.does: Plays the progression (or held chord or drones) in time with the tempo, on the chord length set in Backing. Tapping a chord in Prog mode already starts it, so Play then stops it.

use.text: Tap to start or stop; inverted while playing.
Ctrl+P toggles it from any page.

backplay.recall: Synth page and Backing page, beside the chord pads. Ctrl+P. Ignored while the Track plays.
tips: Backing joins the bar in progress if a beat or loop is already running.
backplay.ask: Why does the backing start when I tap a chord?

chordbeats-.title: BEATS PER CHORD
chordbeats-.summary: How long each chord lasts, in beats.
chordbeats-.does: From 1 to 8 beats; 4 is one bar of 4/4. Shorter means the progression moves faster. Changes how long each slot plays and when arpeggios turn over.

use.text: Tap − or +.

chordbeats-.recall: Backing page, left of the second row of steppers. Default 4.
chordbeats-.ask: How do I make the chords change faster?

arprate-.title: ARP STEPS PER BEAT
arprate-.does: How many notes an arpeggio plays per beat, 1 to 4. At 2 you hear eighth notes. It only changes the Arp styles; Sustain and Pulse ignore it.

use.text: Tap − or +.

arprate-.recall: Backing page, right of Beats per chord. Default 2.
tips: Pulse always plays once per beat, whatever this says.
arprate-.ask: How do I speed up the arpeggio?

bpm2-.title: TEMPO
bpm2-.summary: The tempo in beats per minute.
bpm2-.does: Sets the speed of the beat, backing, loop and track together: 40 to 240 bpm, 1 per tap. It is the same setting as on the Tune and Beat pages.

use.text: Tap − or +.
Ctrl+T taps a tempo.

bpm2-.recall: Backing page, below the progression; also Tune and Beat pages. Ctrl+T.
bpm2-.ask: How do I change the tempo?

backvol.title: BACKING VOLUME
backvol.summary: How loud the backing chords are.
backvol.does: The chords' level, 0 to 100%, separate from the lead and loop. Master volume on System sets the overall level.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar.

backvol.recall: Backing page, right of Tempo. Loop and master volumes are on System.
backvol.ask: How do I make the backing quieter than my lead?

bresync.title: USE CURRENT LEAD SOUND
bresync.summary: Makes the backing play the lead's sound.
bresync.does: The backing keeps the sound it started with, so you can change the lead freely. Tap this when you want the chords to use the sound you are playing now. The line inside shows both names.

use.text: Tap the wide button.

bresync.recall: Backing page, full-width button. The backing otherwise keeps its old sound until cleared and restarted.
bresync.ask: Why does the backing not change when I change my sound?

backing.recall: Backing tab. On Synth the Prog and Play buttons are the same chord controls.

tune.title: Tune
tune.intro: Key, scale, octave, tempo and slide speed: the settings that make everything you play fit together. Listen can guess a song's key.

tab_track.title: PAGE TABS
tab_track.summary: The strip of nine tabs along the top.
tab_track.does: Track, Synth, Sound, Beat, Backing, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_track.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all nine; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_track.ask: What is on each of the pages?

root0.title: KEY (ROOT NOTE)
root0.summary: Pick the home note of your key: C to B.
root0.does: The root is the note the scale is built on and the one the strings return to. Changing it moves every string, chord pad and the bright root frames. All three strings stay locked to the scale.

use.text: Tap one of the twelve notes; the active one is inverted.
Ctrl+K steps up a semitone (Shift added: down).

root0.recall: Tune page, top block; Synth header shows it. Ctrl+K steps up, Ctrl+Shift+K down. Listen can set it too.
tips: Backing chords follow the new key straight away.
root0.ask: How do I choose the right key to play along with a song?

scale0.title: MAJOR
scale0.does: The classic bright scale. Seven notes per octave, so strings have more to choose from and some pairs clash a little if you slide through them.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale0.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

scale1.title: NATURAL MINOR
scale1.does: The standard minor scale: sad, moody, cinematic. Same notes as the major scale that starts a minor third higher.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale1.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.
scale1.ask: When should I use natural minor?

scale2.title: MAJOR PENTATONIC
scale2.summary: Five notes: sweet, hard to get wrong.
scale2.does: Five notes per octave with no tense steps, so almost anything you play sounds pleasant. Country, folk and pop melodies.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale2.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.
scale2.ask: When should I use major pentatonic?

scale3.title: MINOR PENTATONIC
scale3.summary: Five notes: bluesy and rocky. The default.
scale3.does: Five notes of the minor scale with the awkward ones left out. The default scale (A minor pentatonic): good for riffs and solos.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale3.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.
tips: The scale decides which notes the keys give: nothing you press is wrong.
scale3.ask: When should I use minor pentatonic?

scale4.title: BLUES
scale4.summary: Six notes: minor pentatonic plus a blue note.
scale4.does: Adds one gritty in-between note to the minor pentatonic. Sliding through it gives the blues sound.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale4.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

scale5.title: DORIAN
scale5.summary: Seven notes: minor, with a brighter sixth.
scale5.does: A minor-sounding scale with a lifted sixth note: jazzy, folky, hopeful rather than sad.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale5.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

scale6.title: MIXOLYDIAN
scale6.summary: Seven notes: major with a flat seventh.
scale6.does: A major-sounding scale with a lowered seventh: relaxed, bluesy-major, a rock and funk favourite.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale6.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

scale7.title: CHROMATIC
scale7.does: Every semitone, so every key is a half-step from the next and nothing is locked. Notes can clash. Chord pads still use the major scale's chords.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active scale is inverted.
Ctrl+S steps to the next scale; add Shift for previous.

scale7.recall: Tune page, Scale block. Ctrl+S steps forward, Ctrl+Shift+S back. The Synth header shows the short name.

oct-.title: OCTAVE
oct-.summary: Moves the whole instrument up or down in octaves.
oct-.does: Each step shifts every string by 12 semitones, from -3 to +3. Held notes sweep to the new octave without restarting.

use.text: Tap − or +.
Down / Up arrows, or - and =.

oct-.recall: Tune page and Synth page bottom row. Arrows are on the Q20 symbol layer.
oct-.ask: Why do all my notes sound an octave off?

rowint-.title: STRING GAP
rowint-.summary: How far apart the three strings are tuned.
rowint-.does: Semitones between neighbouring strings, 1 to 12 (default 5, a fourth, like a bass or guitar). Lower overlaps the strings; 12 makes each string an octave apart. A semitone is the smallest step on a keyboard.

use.text: Tap − or +.

rowint-.recall: Tune page, middle of the first stepper row. Default 5.
tips: Smaller gaps make chord shapes easier to finger.

bendr-.title: BEND RANGE
bendr-.summary: How far the bend keys move the pitch.
bendr-.does: Holding Left or Right bends the pitch down or up by up to this many semitones (1 to 12, default 2) with a short ramp. Also the reach of the Bend touch pad mapping's left-right axis.

use.text: Tap − or +.
Hold Left / Right (or [ ]) to bend.

bendr-.recall: Tune page, third stepper of the first row. Default 2.
tips: 12 gives a full octave of bend.
bendr-.ask: How do I get a bigger pitch bend?

bpm-.title: TEMPO
bpm-.summary: The tempo in beats per minute (bpm).
bpm-.does: Sets the speed of beat, backing, loop and track together: 40 to 240 bpm, one per tap here. Delay times and the metronome follow it.

use.text: Tap − or +.
Ctrl+T: tap in time.

bpm-.recall: Tune page; the Backing and Beat pages have the same control in steps of 2. Ctrl+T taps a tempo.
bpm-.ask: How do I match the tempo of a song?

tap.title: TAP
tap.summary: Sets the tempo by tapping it.
tap.does: Tap in time a few times: it averages your last six taps (a pause over two seconds starts afresh) and sets the tempo to match. At least two taps are needed.

use.text: Tap steadily on the button.
Ctrl+T from any page.

tap.recall: Tune page, middle of the tempo row. Ctrl+T works anywhere. Fix errors with the Tempo stepper.

metro.title: CLICK
metro.summary: The metronome: a click on every beat.
metro.does: A soft click in time with the tempo, accented on beat one of each bar. Loop count-ins and Beat Rec click regardless.

use.text: Tap to switch on or off; inverted means on.
Ctrl+M.

metro.recall: Tune page and Backing page (Metronome); Ctrl+M anywhere.
metro.ask: How do I play along with a click?

glidescale.title: GLIDE SPEED
glidescale.summary: Makes every slide faster or slower.
glidescale.does: A multiplier on each sound's own glide time (how long slides take): all the way left is instant jumps, the default is x1.00, and the far right is four times slower. It affects all sounds at once.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar. Left reads instant.

glidescale.recall: Tune page, right of Tap and Click. Default is x1.00 (a quarter of the way along).
tips: A sound's own GLIDE (Sound > All parameters) is the starting point.
glidescale.ask: How do I make slides snappier or slower?

listen.title: LISTEN
listen.summary: Listens for six seconds and guesses key and tempo.
listen.does: Records from the system's default audio input, then estimates the key and tempo of music playing nearby, with a likely/guess/unsure rating. This Hackberry has no microphone, so it will say so.

use.text: Tap Listen and hold the source near the mic.

listen.recall: Tune page, Listen box at the bottom. Nothing changes until you tap Use key, Use tempo or Use both.
tips: Always check the result by ear: detection is an estimate.
listen.ask: What does Listen need to work?

lkey.title: USE KEY
lkey.does: Sets the key's root note and switches to major or minor to match. If you were on a pentatonic scale it stays pentatonic (major or minor). Tempo is not touched.

use.text: Tap Use key after a result appears.

lkey.recall: Tune page, after Listen returns a result. Change it back in the Key and Scale blocks.

ltempo.title: USE TEMPO
ltempo.does: Sets the tempo to the detected bpm, if a pulse was found. The key and scale are left alone.

use.text: Tap Use tempo after a result appears.

ltempo.recall: Tune page, after Listen returns a result. Fix by hand with Tempo or Tap.

lboth.title: USE BOTH
lboth.summary: Applies both the key and the tempo.
lboth.does: Does Use key and Use tempo together in one tap, so you can play along with what you just listened to.

use.text: Tap Use both after a result appears.

lboth.recall: Tune page, after Listen returns a result. Undo by choosing the key, scale and tempo by hand.
lboth.ask: Should I use both the key and tempo?

lnext.title: OTHER KEY
lnext.summary: Shows Listen's next best key guess.
lnext.does: Listen keeps its three best key guesses; the first is the most likely. Tap to cycle through guess 1, 2 and 3, then Use key applies the one shown.

use.text: Tap to step to the next guess.

lnext.recall: Tune page, after Listen returns a result. The button says which guess (1 of 3) is shown.
tips: The second and third guesses are rated half as sure.
lnext.ask: What if Listen picks the wrong key?

tune.recall: Tune tab, or tap the key, tempo or octave readout at the top of Synth.

system.title: System
system.intro: Master volume, touch pad mapping, recording and saving, key test, device status, and Panic.

tab_track.title: PAGE TABS
tab_track.summary: The strip of nine tabs along the top.
tab_track.does: Track, Synth, Sound, Beat, Backing, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_track.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all nine; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_track.ask: What is on each of the pages?

volume.title: MASTER VOLUME
volume.does: Sets the final loudness of everything, 0 to 100%. A limiter means the output can never exceed full scale, but a Limit tag shows when it is holding sound back.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar.

volume.recall: System page, top left. Beat, backing and loop have their own sliders; sound LEVEL is separate.
tips: If the sound is distorted or quiet with Limit showing, lower this.
volume.ask: Why is it quiet, or why does Limit show?

loopvol.title: LOOP VOLUME
loopvol.summary: How loud the recorded loop is.
loopvol.does: Level of the loop pedal's layers, 0 to 100%, separate from what you play live.

use.text: Tap or drag along the bar.

loopvol.recall: System page, top right. Loop pedal itself is on the Synth page.
loopvol.ask: How do I balance the loop against my playing?

xymap0.title: FILTER MAPPING
xymap0.summary: Touch pad pair: Cutoff and resonance.
xymap0.does: X is cutoff (dark to bright), Y is resonance (a whistling edge). Drag to sweep the filter like a classic synth knob pair.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap0.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap0.ask: What does the filter mapping do?

xymap1.title: WOBBLE MAPPING
xymap1.summary: Touch pad pair: Cutoff and vibrato.
xymap1.does: X is cutoff, Y adds vibrato (pitch wobble). Drag up for a wobble, sideways to open or close the sound.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap1.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap1.ask: What does the wobble mapping do?

xymap2.title: MORPH MAPPING
xymap2.summary: Touch pad pair: Timbre and drive.
xymap2.does: X blends in the second oscillator (timbre, the tone colour), Y adds drive (distortion). Moves the sound from plain to rich and gritty.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap2.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap2.ask: What does the morph mapping do?

xymap3.title: SPACE MAPPING
xymap3.summary: Touch pad pair: Delay and reverb.
xymap3.does: X adds echoes (delay), Y adds room sound (reverb). Makes the sound drift away to the right and upward.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap3.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap3.ask: What does the space mapping do?

xymap4.title: BEND MAPPING
xymap4.summary: Touch pad pair: Pitch and cutoff.
xymap4.does: X bends pitch down or up (by the Bend range), Y moves cutoff. Centre is no bend. Good for dive bombs and rising wails.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap4.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
xymap4.ask: What does the bend mapping do?

xymap5.title: GLITCH MAPPING
xymap5.summary: Touch pad pair: Coarse and grit.
xymap5.does: Crushes everything you hear into a rough digital sound: X is coarse (blockier, metallic), Y is grit (rougher, noisier). Coloured streaks trail the wave.

use.text: Tap to choose it; the active mapping is inverted.
Ctrl+G steps to the next mapping from any page.

xymap5.recall: System page, Touch pad mapping row; Synth page scope corner. Ctrl+G steps on. Panic clears Glitch.
tips: Glitch affects lead, backing, loop and drums together.
xymap5.ask: What does the glitch mapping do?

xyhold2.title: HOLD
xyhold2.summary: Keeps the pad's last position after you lift.
xyhold2.does: Off: the sound returns to normal on release. On: the touch pad's last position stays applied until you turn Hold off or touch the pad again. Same switch as on the Synth page's scope.

use.text: Tap to switch; inverted means on.

xyhold2.recall: System page, end of the mapping row; Synth page scope corner.
xyhold2.ask: Why does my touch pad effect stay on?

chordrow.title: CHORD ROW
chordrow.summary: The bottom letter row plays chords, not notes.
chordrow.does: On: Z to M play backing chords I to VII instead of the low string, and labels show on those keys. Off: it is a string again. The Alt key does the same while held.

use.text: Tap to switch; inverted means on.
$ toggles it; hold Alt + Z..M for a single chord.

chordrow.recall: System page, first button below the mapping row. $ toggles it; the toast says which state.
tips: The Beat page keeps the bottom row as the low string.
chordrow.ask: How do I play chords from the keyboard?

recwav.title: RECORD
recwav.summary: Records what you hear to a WAV file.
recwav.does: Starts recording the full output (lead, backing, loop, beat) into a WAV audio file in recordings/. Press again to stop; the file name shows. A REC timer blinks on the Synth page.

use.text: Tap Record, play, then tap Stop rec.
Ctrl+E starts and stops.

recwav.recall: System page; Ctrl+E anywhere. Files are in ~/vrequency/recordings/. Play last plays the newest.
tips: Only the Track page's Export renders offline; Record is real time.
recwav.ask: How do I record a take?

playlast.title: PLAY LAST
playlast.summary: Plays your newest recording through the speaker.
playlast.does: Plays the most recent file in recordings/ with the system player (pw-play or aplay). The same button stops it. You can play along while it runs. It cannot choose older files.

use.text: Tap Play last; tap again to stop.
Ctrl+W.

playlast.recall: System page; Ctrl+W anywhere. It also plays an exported track, since that is the newest file.
playlast.ask: How do I hear my last recording?

savesession.title: SAVE SESSION
savesession.summary: Saves the whole setup as a session file.
savesession.does: Writes your sounds, key, tempo, backing, loop, the beat shown and the track into a timestamped file in sessions/. It does not stop anything. The list below shows the four newest.

use.text: Tap Save session; a toast shows the file name.

savesession.recall: System page. Load from the list below the buttons, then press play on the loop, backing or beat.
tips: Quitting saves your setup automatically; sessions are for keeping versions.

keytest.title: KEY TEST
keytest.summary: Shows which keys the keyboard reports.
keytest.does: Opens a panel that lists every key you hold and the most you held at once. Use it to check that the keyboard can read several keys together (chords) without ghosting, which is a hardware limit.

use.text: Tap Key test to open; Close (or Esc) to leave.

keytest.recall: System page, last button of the row. Esc also closes it and goes to Synth.
keytest.ask: How many keys can my keyboard read at once?

session0.title: SAVED SESSIONS
session0.summary: Your four newest sessions. Tap to load one.
session0.does: Loads that session: sounds, key, tempo, backing, loop, the beat shown and the track replace what you have. Sounds do not start by themselves; press play on the loop, backing or beat.

use.text: Tap a session name. A toast confirms.

session0.recall: System page, Saved sessions. Only the four newest show. Save first if you want to keep your current setup.
tips: Loading replaces the track too, but the track's own undo can bring it back.
session0.ask: What happens when I load a session?

panic.title: PANIC
panic.does: Silences all notes and stops the backing, beat, loop playback and the track. Clears Glitch and sustain. A loop being recorded is dropped; a finished loop is kept. Use it when a note sticks.

use.text: Tap Panic.
Backspace from any page.

panic.recall: System page, bottom left; Backspace anywhere. On the Track page Backspace deletes a chosen clip instead.
panic.ask: A note is stuck. How do I stop everything?

latency-.title: LOOP FIX
latency-.summary: Moves recorded loops and beats earlier or later.
latency-.does: Milliseconds, 0 to 500 in steps of 10. Bluetooth speakers play about 0.2 s behind your fingers, so your recording lands late; this shifts recorded hits earlier to match. Raise it if hits land late, lower it if early.

use.text: Tap − or +, record a bar and listen.

latency-.recall: System page, bottom row. Set to 200 automatically for Bluetooth outputs; 0 for others.
tips: Live playing keeps its delay; only recordings are corrected.
latency-.ask: My loops play late. How do I fix the timing?

factory.title: FACTORY SOUNDS
factory.summary: Restores slots 1-0 and the dream sounds.
factory.does: Puts the ten original sounds back in the slots, replacing anything you stored, and re-adds any of the five dream sounds you deleted. Your own favourites stay.

use.text: Tap Factory sounds. A toast reports what returned.

factory.recall: System page, bottom row. This overwrites slots 1-0 and cannot be undone.
factory.ask: How do I get the original sounds back?

quit.title: QUIT
quit.summary: Saves your setup and closes the app.
quit.does: Quits venv-vrequency. Your sounds, key, tempo, settings, kept beats and track are saved first and come back next time.

use.text: Tap Quit.
Ctrl+Q.

quit.recall: System page, bottom right; Ctrl+Q anywhere. Reopen from the app grid.

system.recall: System tab. Ctrl+E records what you hear; Ctrl+W plays the last recording.

key-test.title: Key test
key-test.intro: A panel over the System page that shows live which keys the keyboard reports, and how many it reads at once.

keytestclose.title: CLOSE KEY TEST
keytestclose.does: The panel lists the keys held now, the most held at once, and the last twelve down and up events. A key you did not press showing up, or a pressed key missing, is a keyboard limit, not a synth fault.

use.text: Tap Close.
Esc closes it and returns to Synth.

keytestclose.recall: Open from System page, Key test. Hold one key on each row then add more to find the limit.
tips: Most keys held at once is the number to report.
keytestclose.ask: What am I supposed to look for in Key test?

key-test.recall: System tab, Key test button. Close or Esc leaves it.

help.title: Help
help.intro: The key lists built into the app: four pages for playing, commands, the beat and the Track. The list follows your keymap.

tab_track.title: PAGE TABS
tab_track.summary: The strip of nine tabs along the top.
tab_track.does: Track, Synth, Sound, Beat, Backing, Tune, System, Help and Chat. The page you are on is inverted. Chat shows how many copilot messages are unread. The Synth page has no strip: Menu or any tab brings you here.

use.text: Tap a tab to go there.
Tab steps to the next page; Esc goes to Synth.

tab_track.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all nine; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_track.ask: What is on each of the pages?

help_next.title: HELP PAGE BUTTON
help_next.summary: Cycles through the four key lists.
help_next.does: The Help page lists keys in four pages: Playing, Commands (hold Ctrl), Beat and recording, and Track. Each tap moves on to the next page, then wraps back to Playing.

use.text: Tap to step to the next list.

help_next.recall: Help tab, bottom left. Ctrl+H opens Help from any page and closes it again.
tips: The bindings shown follow your keymap.json.
help_next.ask: Where do I find every keyboard shortcut?

help_back.title: BACK TO PLAYING
help_back.does: Leaves Help and goes straight to the instrument. Esc does the same from any page.

use.text: Tap Back to playing.
Esc, or Ctrl+H to close Help.

help_back.ask: How do I get back to the instrument?

help_section.title: SECTION TITLE
help_section.summary: Names which of the four key lists you are reading.
help_section.does: Help has four lists: Playing, Commands, Beat and recording, and Track. The title says which one is open; Next steps to the following list.

use.text: Read only. Use the Next button to change list.

help_section.recall: Top left of the Help page.
help_section.ask: Which key list should I read first?

help_tour.title: TOUR
help_tour.summary: Opens this tour: a picture of every page you can tap.
help_tour.does: Starts the interactive tour. It never changes your sound or settings; it only draws pictures and reads help cards. Tap a control to read what it does.

use.text: Tap Tour. Then tap any control in the picture.
Ctrl+O opens the tour from any page; Esc leaves it.

help_tour.recall: Help page, top row. Or Ctrl+O from any page, or ask Rook to show you.
tips: The tour remembers the page you were on last.
help_tour.ask: Can you show me around the app?

help_ask.title: ASK ROOK
help_ask.summary: Opens a chat with Rook, ready to ask about this guide.
help_ask.does: Opens the chat dock with a question started for you. Rook can answer here and point at controls on the screen.

use.text: Tap it, or tap any key row to ask about that row.
Ctrl+Y opens the chat dock on any page.

help_ask.recall: Help page, top right. Ctrl+Y from any page.
tips: Esc hands the keys back to the page.
help_ask.ask: Who is Rook and what can they do?

help.recall: Help tab, or Ctrl+H from anywhere. Ctrl+H again leaves it.

tab_track.recall: Top of every page except Synth. Tab cycles forward through all nine; Esc returns to Synth.
tips: Ctrl+H toggles Help and Ctrl+Y toggles Chat from anywhere.
tab_track.ask: What is on each of the pages?

chat_history.title: CHAT HISTORY
chat_history.does: Messages from the copilot (white name tag) and from you (outlined YOU). A ? after a name means it is asking you something; tip marks a suggestion. The top right says whether a copilot is listening. The last 200 are kept.

use.text: Drag up or down to scroll.
Up / Down (or PageUp / PageDown) scroll.

chat_history.recall: Chat tab; Ctrl+Y jumps here from any page and back. Esc leaves.
tips: New messages on other pages appear in a strip at the bottom for a few seconds.
chat_history.ask: How does the copilot see what I am playing?

chat_send.title: SEND
chat_send.does: Sends the text in the box to the copilot. On this page letters type instead of playing strings; Enter sends, Backspace deletes. Messages wait for a copilot if none is connected.

use.text: Tap Send.
Enter sends; Backspace deletes a letter.

chat_send.recall: Chat tab, bottom right. Ctrl+Y toggles the page; Tab and Ctrl shortcuts still work.
tips: Hold Shift for capital letters; the symbol layer gives digits and punctuation.
chat_send.ask: How do I type to the copilot?

chat_input.title: MESSAGE BOX
chat_input.summary: Where your message to Rook appears as you type.
chat_input.does: On this page the letter keys type instead of playing. Enter sends; Backspace edits. A cursor blinks while you can type. Messages carry where you were when you sent them.

use.text: Just type, then press Enter to send.
Tap Send to send; the keyboard does the typing.

chat_input.recall: Chat tab, bottom. Ctrl+Shift+Y jumps here from any page.
tips: Esc leaves the page and plays again.
chat_input.ask: What can I ask you to do?

chat.recall: Chat tab, or Ctrl+Shift+Y from anywhere. Ctrl+Y opens a small chat dock instead.

recall.title: RECALL
recall.summary: How to get back to anything you changed.
recall.does: Every card ends with a Recall line: where the control lives, its shortcut, and how to undo or reset it. Sounds come back from slots (1-0), favourites or Ctrl+Z; setups from sessions; a stuck mess from Panic.

use.text: Read the Recall line on any card to find the page and shortcut.
Ctrl+Z undoes the last sound change; Backspace is Panic.
Tap a slot or favourite to bring a sound back; System lists sessions.

recall.recall: Help tab, Ctrl+H, lists every key. Esc returns to Synth from anywhere.
tips: Not everything is undoable: Store to a slot and Delete are final.
recall.ask: How do I get back a sound or setting I lost?

scale-lock.title: SCALE LOCK
scale-lock.summary: Every key plays a note that fits the key and scale.
scale-lock.does: You pick a root note and a scale (a set of notes that sound good together). The strings only offer those notes, so nothing is a wrong note. Left to right goes up the scale. Hold Shift for chromatic: every semitone, off the scale.

use.text: Tune page: tap a root note, then a scale.
Ctrl+K key up, Ctrl+S next scale, hold Shift for semitones.

scale-lock.recall: Tune page, Key and Scale; header on the Synth page shows both. Default is A minor pentatonic.
tips: Pentatonic scales have five notes and are the hardest to get wrong.
scale-lock.ask: Why can I not play a wrong note?

strings.title: THE THREE STRINGS
strings.summary: Each letter row is a string that plays one note at a time.
strings.does: High string Q to P, middle A to L, low Z to M. Each is monophonic: one note at a time, like a real string. The strings are tuned a gap apart (5 semitones by default) so shapes across rows make chords.

use.text: Press a letter; hold shapes across rows for chords.
Press a note; drag to slide.

strings.recall: Synth page, the three strings. Tune page, String gap changes the spacing.
tips: On Track, letters are commands: Esc returns.
strings.ask: How are the three strings laid out?

slides.title: SLIDES (GLIDE)
slides.summary: A second key on a held string slides the note.
slides.does: Hold one key and press another on the same row: the pitch glides to the new note without restarting (no new attack). Release the newer key and it glides back. The glide time is the sound's GLIDE setting times Tune's Glide speed.

use.text: Hold A, press F, release F.
Press a note on the string and drag sideways.
Hold a shape across rows and re-finger it: the chord glides.

slides.recall: Synth page strings. Slide time: Tune > Glide speed, or Sound > All parameters > GLIDE.
tips: Sustain makes slides smoother: new keys slide the ringing note.
slides.ask: How do I make the note slide?

loop-pedal.title: LOOP PEDAL FLOW
loop-pedal.summary: One button: count in, record, play, layer.
loop-pedal.does: 1 Tap Loop: count-in. 2 Play: it records notes, slides, bends and pad moves. 3 Tap: recording ends at the bar's end, then it loops. 4 Tap: add a layer (DUB). 5 Tap: finish it. Up to six layers, 64 bars; each layer keeps its sound.

use.text: Tap Loop; the label always says what the next tap does.
Enter; Ctrl+U undo layer, Ctrl+L play/stop, Ctrl+D clear.

loop-pedal.recall: Synth page, bottom left. Loop volume: System. Loops late? System > Loop fix.
tips: The loop records notes, not audio, so it follows tempo changes.
loop-pedal.ask: How do I record my first loop?

bar-lines.title: BAR LINES AND QUANTISE
bar-lines.summary: Things start and change on the bar so they stay in time.
bar-lines.does: A bar is a group of beats (4 here). The beat, backing, loop and track share bar lines. Recorded loops end on a bar; a beat you tap waits for the next bar; drum hits are quantised: snapped to the nearest of 16 steps in the bar.

use.text: Start things in any order: they join the bar in progress.

bar-lines.recall: Tempo: Tune page. Bluetooth timing: System > Loop fix. Metronome: Ctrl+M.
tips: Metronome: Ctrl+M, or Click on the Tune page.
bar-lines.ask: Why do things wait for the next bar?

sessions-favourites-state.title: SESSIONS, FAVOURITES, SETUP
sessions-favourites-state.summary: Three ways your work is kept.
sessions-favourites-state.does: Your setup (slots, key, tempo, settings, kept beats, track) saves itself on quit. A favourite is one saved sound. A session is a snapshot: sounds, key, tempo, backing, loop, the beat shown and the track.

use.text: Sound page: Save. System page: Save session, tap one to load.
Ctrl+F saves a favourite.

sessions-favourites-state.recall: Files live in ~/vrequency/: state.json, favourites/, sessions/, recordings/. Delete keymap.json to reset keys.
tips: Sessions list shows the four newest.
sessions-favourites-state.ask: What is the difference between a favourite, a session and my setup?

command-layer.title: COMMAND LAYER (CTRL)
command-layer.summary: Hold Ctrl and press a letter for a command instead of a note.
command-layer.does: Ctrl is the command key. Held, letters run actions: R new sound, N mutate, Z undo, F favourite, K key up, S scale, T tap tempo, M click, G pad mapping, E record, W play last, H help, Y chat, Q quit. Some change on the Track page.

use.text: Hold Ctrl, press the letter. Shift reverses K and S.

command-layer.recall: Help tab, Commands page lists them all. Edit keymap.json to rebind; delete it to reset.
tips: On Track: Ctrl+T split, J join, R repeat, X/C/V cut copy paste, B export.

q20-layers.title: Q20 KEYBOARD LAYERS
q20-layers.summary: Arrows and digits sit on the Q20's symbol and number layers.
q20-layers.does: The Q20 keyboard puts digits (1-9, 0 pick sounds) on a number layer and arrows (bend, octave) on a symbol layer. [ ] also bend and - = also change octave. Alt is the chord layer, Ctrl the command layer, $ toggles chord row.

use.text: Use the layer key, then the digit or arrow.
Backspace is Panic, Enter the loop pedal, Tab next page, Esc home.

q20-layers.recall: Help tab shows the keys. System > Key test shows exactly what the keyboard reports.
tips: Key test is the way to check which keys reach the app.
q20-layers.ask: Where are the arrow keys and numbers on the Q20?

xy-mappings.title: TOUCH PAD MAPPINGS
xy-mappings.summary: Six pairs of controls for the scope pad.
xy-mappings.does: Filter: cutoff and reso. Wobble: cutoff and vibrato. Morph: timbre and drive. Space: delay and reverb. Bend: pitch and cutoff. Glitch: coarse and grit (crushes everything). X is left-right, Y is bottom-top.

use.text: Drag on the scope; pick the pair with the corner button.
Ctrl+G steps through them.

xy-mappings.recall: Synth page scope corner; System page row of six. Hold keeps the position.
tips: Moves are recorded into the loop while it records.
xy-mappings.ask: Which touch pad mapping should I use?

glitch.title: GLITCH
glitch.summary: Crushes everything you hear into a rough digital sound.
glitch.does: While your finger is on the pad (or Hold is on) lead, backing, loop and drums are crushed into a blocky, lo-fi sound. Right is coarser, up is rougher. Coloured streaks trail the scope wave. Lift to restore; Backspace clears it.

use.text: Choose Glitch, drag on the scope.
Backspace switches it off.

glitch.recall: Synth page scope corner, or System page, Glitch. Lift your finger to end it.
glitch.ask: What does Glitch do to my sound?

backing-modes.title: BACKING MODES
backing-modes.summary: What a chord tap does: Prog, Hold or Drone.
backing-modes.does: Prog queues up to eight chords that loop, each lasting its Beats per chord. Hold plays one chord until you pick another. Drone switches held bass notes on and off. A chord tap in Prog starts the backing at once.

use.text: Tap the mode button beside the chord pads.
Ctrl+B changes mode; Alt + Z..M plays a chord.

backing-modes.recall: Backing page, three buttons at the top. Ctrl+X clears the backing.
tips: The backing keeps the sound it started with; use Use current lead sound to match.
backing-modes.ask: How do I build a chord progression?

kept-beats.title: KEPT BEATS
kept-beats.summary: A row of beats you can switch between.
kept-beats.does: Every beat you make is kept in the Beats row, like patterns of a drum machine. + New starts a fresh one. Switching while playing waits for the next bar line. Each has its own kit; tempo and volume are shared. Saved as you go.

use.text: Tap a beat; use More for older beats.
Left / Right on the Beat page.

kept-beats.recall: Beat page, row under the pads. Beats cannot be deleted or renamed yet.
kept-beats.ask: How do I keep more than one beat?

track-flow.title: TRACK: CLIPS, LANES, BARS
track-flow.summary: Make something, keep it, place it, play it, export it.
track-flow.does: 1 Make a beat, chords or a loop. 2 Track tab: + Keep. 3 Tap a clip on the shelf, then a bar in its lane. 4 Split, chop, mute, repeat, change sound, mix. 5 Play, then Export to a WAV.

use.text: Shelf, then lane. Tap a placed clip to choose; drag to move.
Space plays, K keeps, E chops, I sound, X mix, Ctrl+B exports.

track-flow.recall: Track tab. Ctrl+Space plays from any page. Ctrl+Z undoes (40 steps).
tips: Letters are commands on this page; Esc returns to Synth.
track-flow.ask: How do I turn my beat and loop into a song?

scope-readouts.title: SCOPE READOUTS
scope-readouts.summary: The numbers around the scope describe the real output.
scope-readouts.does: Top: volts and time per division (they follow the signal), trigger state and sample rate. Bottom: frequency, peak-to-peak level and note. They never change the sound.

use.text: Read them; the scope itself is the touch pad.

scope-readouts.recall: Synth page. Faint X and Y labels name the pad's axes.
tips: Frequency reads an octave low on sounds with a SUB: that is the wave's true repeat rate.
scope-readouts.ask: What are the numbers on the scope?

level-strip.title: LEVEL STRIP
level-strip.summary: A row of segments showing output loudness.
level-strip.does: 86 small segments under the header light up with the loudness of what you hear (output level). When the limiter is holding the sound back, a Limit tag shows beside the sound name. It is only a display; tapping does nothing.

use.text: Watch it; lower Master volume if it pegs.

level-strip.recall: Synth page, thin strip under the header. Master volume: System page.
level-strip.ask: How do I tell if the sound is too loud?

string-brackets.title: STRING BRACKETS
string-brackets.summary: Brackets that show where the pitch really is.
string-brackets.does: While a string sounds, a line wobbles across it and a pair of brackets sits round the true pitch, with a short trail. During a slide the brackets travel between note boxes. Boxes with bright frames are the key's root note.

use.text: Slide a note and watch the brackets.

string-brackets.ask: What are the brackets on the strings?

adsr.title: ADSR ENVELOPE
adsr.summary: Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release: the shape of a note's volume.
adsr.does: Attack: how fast a note fades in. Decay: how fast it falls to Sustain, the level held while the key is down. Release: the fade after you let go.

use.text: Sound page: Attack and Release; All parameters for Decay and Sustain.

adsr.recall: Sound page: Attack, Release. All parameters: Decay, Sustain.
tips: The filter has its own envelope: F.ATK, F.DEC, F.SUS, F.REL.
adsr.ask: What do attack, decay, sustain and release do?

panic.title: PANIC
panic.does: Stops all notes, the backing, beat, loop playback and track, and clears Glitch and sustain. A loop being recorded is dropped; a finished loop is kept. On the Track page Backspace first deletes a chosen clip.

use.text: Backspace from any page.
System page, Panic.

panic.recall: System page, Panic; Backspace anywhere. Ctrl+L restarts the loop; chord taps restart the backing.
panic.ask: Everything is stuck. What do I press?

tempo.title: TEMPO (BPM)
tempo.summary: One tempo for the beat, backing, loop and track.
tempo.does: Beats per minute, 40 to 240, shared by everything: backing, beat, loop and track, plus delay times and the metronome. It appears on the Synth header, and on the Tune (steps of 1), Backing and Beat pages (steps of 2).

use.text: Tune page: − / + or Tap.
Ctrl+T taps a tempo; Ctrl+M clicks.

tempo.recall: Tune page; Ctrl+T anywhere. The beat lamp in the Synth header flashes on each beat while something plays.
tempo.ask: How do I set the tempo?

copilot.title: THE COPILOT (ROOK)
copilot.summary: An AI helper that can play and edit the app with you.
copilot.does: A copilot connects through a local control socket (off with --no-control). It can play notes, change the sound, set a beat or backing, and look at the screen. Its messages show in Chat, or in a strip at the bottom of any page.

use.text: Ctrl+Y jumps to Chat and back; type and press Enter.
Chat tab, type, tap Send.

copilot.recall: Chat tab; Ctrl+Y. The Chat tab shows an unread count. The strip never takes keys or touch.
tips: copilot: listening at the top right means one is connected.
copilot.ask: What can the copilot do for me?

undo-map.title: WHAT UNDOES WHAT
undo-map.summary: Each part of the app has its own undo.
undo-map.does: Sounds: Ctrl+Z (24 steps): New, Mutate, slots, favourites; not slider moves or Store. Loop: Ctrl+U per layer. Track: Ctrl+Z on the Track page (40 steps; Shift for redo). Backing: Remove last or Clear. Beat: Erase.

use.text: Ctrl+Z (Sound or Track), Ctrl+U (loop).
Undo buttons on Sound, Synth and Track pages.

undo-map.recall: Sound page Undo; Synth page Undo (loop); Track page Undo. Final: Store, Delete, deleting a shelf clip.
tips: Ctrl+Z means sound undo everywhere except the Track page.

ticker.title: THE TICKER
ticker.summary: Copilot messages appear over the bottom of any page.
ticker.does: A new copilot message shows in a two-line strip near the bottom for about seven seconds while you are on another page, and the Chat tab counts unread messages. It covers the bottom row of controls but takes no taps or keys.

use.text: Keep playing; open Chat to read and answer.

ticker.recall: Chat tab holds the full conversation. Ctrl+Y jumps there.
ticker.ask: Why did a message appear over my buttons?

step-grid.title: STEP GRID
step-grid.summary: The 8 x 16 picture of every drum hit in the beat bar.
step-grid.does: Eight rows (one per drum) by sixteen columns (the steps of one bar). A lit cell is a hit; a line sweeps across while the beat plays. It is a display: you write hits by playing the pads.

use.text: Read only. Tap a pad, with Rec on, to write a hit on the nearest step.

tips: Erase then a pad clears that drum row.
step-grid.ask: How do I write a beat?

status-box.title: STATUS BOX
status-box.summary: Facts about the audio output and the engine.
status-box.does: Shows the audio backend, sample rate, block size, output device, engine load, late blocks, the data folder and the last recording. If it says No real audio device, nothing will be heard.

use.text: Read only. Useful when sound stops or crackles.

status-box.recall: System page, the framed box in the middle.
tips: Late blocks above 0 mean the sound broke up.

listen-result.title: LISTEN RESULT
listen-result.summary: The key and tempo Listen guessed, with how sure it is.
listen-result.does: After Listen hears music it shows the most likely key and scale, the tempo, and a confidence for each. Low confidence means a guess. Use key, use tempo or use both to apply.

use.text: Tap Use key, Use tempo or Use both; Other key tries the next guess.

tips: Detection is an estimate: check by ear.
listen-result.ask: How good is the key detection?

help-rows.title: KEY LIST ROWS
help-rows.summary: A key (left) and what it does (right), for your keymap.
help-rows.does: Each row names a key or key combination and says what it does. The list follows your keymap, so if you remapped keys it shows your keys. Four lists: playing, commands, beat, track.

use.text: Tap a row to ask Rook about it.
Tap Next to read the next list.

tips: Q20 digits and arrows are on its number and symbol layers.

tour.title: THE TOUR
tour.summary: A picture of each page where every control explains itself.
tour.does: The tour shows a still picture of a page. Tap a control, or move with the arrow keys, and a card says what it does, how to use it by touch and keys, and how to find it again. Nothing in it is live.

use.text: Tap a control in the picture. Tap empty space to clear. Tabs at the top change page.
Arrows move, Tab cycles, Enter asks Rook, comma and period change page, Esc leaves.

tour.recall: Help page, Tour button. Ctrl+O from any page. Or ask Rook to show you.
tips: Start here walks through every page in order.
tour.ask: Can you walk me through the tour?
